label: Sixth-edition aphorisms
title: Aphorism § 113
text:
§ 113



 The only exceptions to this are the narcotic medicines. As they, in
          their primary action, take away sometimes the sensibility and sensation, sometimes the
          irritability, it frequently happens that in their secondary action, even from moderate
          experimental doses on healthy bodies, an increased sensibility (and a greater
          irritability) is observable.
